content.user_title: Audit Code for Common Security Flaws
content.value_statement: Security bugs can appear in database, shell, file, and error-handling code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused checks and clear remediation.
actual_capabilities: Identifies SQL injection patterns and recommends parameterized queries.
Flags unsafe shell execution patterns and safer subprocess usage.
Reviews broad exception handling and suggests specific exception types.
Checks examples for hardcoded secrets, XSS, and path traversal risks.
Produces severity-based audit notes with remediation guidance.
limitations: It provides review guidance, not a complete automated scanner.
It does not run dynamic security tests by itself.
Findings still require project context and human validation.
It does not prove regulatory compliance or production readiness.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Audit database queries, shell calls, file access, and error handling before merge.

use_cases.title: Standardize Security Checks
use_cases.description: Use consistent OWASP-focused review prompts across teams and repositories.

use_cases.title: Prepare Remediation Plans
use_cases.description: Convert risky patterns into prioritized fixes with safer implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed files for common security flaws. Focus on SQL injection, shell injection, path traversal, XSS, secrets, and exception handling.

prompt_templates.title: Database Query Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit database query construction in this repository. Identify unsafe interpolation, concatenation, raw query use, and missing parameterization.

prompt_templates.title: Command Execution Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review command execution paths. Flag shell usage, user-controlled arguments, weak validation, and safer alternatives for each risky command.

prompt_templates.title: Release Security Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release security audit. Prioritize exploitable issues, cite affected files, explain impact, and give concrete remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request that adds user search and export features.
output: High: User search builds a query from request data without parameterization.
Medium: Export path uses a user-provided filename without path containment checks.
Recommendation: Use parameterized queries and resolve paths against an allowed directory.

output_examples.input: Audit a service that launches command-line tools from API input.
output: Critical: User input reaches shell command construction without validation.
Recommendation: Avoid shell mode, pass fixed arguments as a list, and validate allowed values.

output_examples.input: Check exception handling in a data ingestion job.
output: Medium: Broad exception handling hides parsing and network failures.
Recommendation: Catch specific errors, log useful context, and re-raise unexpected failures.

best_practices: Review security-sensitive areas first, including authentication, database access, file handling, and command execution.
Treat every finding as a hypothesis until code context confirms exploitability.
Pair each confirmed issue with a concrete safer pattern and test recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not report regex matches without checking nearby code and intent.
Do not treat educational bad examples as production vulnerabilities.
Do not ignore low-severity issues when they combine into a real attack path.

faq.question: Does this skill replace a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It guides human and AI review and can complement scanners such as SAST and dependency tools.

faq.question: Which vulnerability classes does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers SQL injection, shell injection, path traversal, XSS, hardcoded secrets, and broad exception handling.

faq.question: Can it review any programming language?
faq.answer: It is framework-generic, but its strongest examples focus on Python, TypeScript, SQL, and common web patterns.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides review instructions and examples. Users decide whether to run any local tools.

faq.question: How should teams use the results?
faq.answer: Use the findings to prioritize remediation, request code changes, and add targeted tests before release.

faq.question: Can it prove that code is secure?
faq.answer: No. It reduces missed issues, but security still needs testing, threat modeling, and review by qualified people.
